descripcion_es: Predictions, offers, promises and decisions made on the spot.
resumen: Will + infinitive is used for predictions based on opinion, decisions made at the moment of speaking, offers and promises. Its form is the same for all persons.

items: Prediction or opinion about the future, often with I think, probably, I'm sure: I think Spain will win.
Spontaneous decision: The phone's ringing. I'll answer it.
Offer: I'll carry that bag for you.
Request: Will you close the door, please?

explicacion.texto: Difference from going to: if the decision was already made before speaking, use going to (I'm going to buy a bike; I've seen one I like). If you decide at the moment, use will (Oh, it's cheap. I'll buy it).
After will comes the infinitive without to and without -s: She will come, not She will comes or She will to come.
With I think, the negative usually goes on think: I don't think it will rain (better than I think it won't rain).

ejemplos.frase: Don't worry, I'll pay for the coffee.
ejemplos.traduccion: No te preocupes, yo pago los cafés.

ejemplos.frase: I'm sure you'll pass the exam.
Prices will probably go up next year.
ejemplos.traduccion: Probablemente los precios subirán el año que viene.

ejemplos.frase: I promise I won't be late.
ejemplos.traduccion: Te prometo que no llegaré tarde.

ejemplos.frase: Shall we go for a walk?

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I help you with that box.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I'll help you with that box.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In Spanish you offer with the present (“te ayudo”); in English, with will.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: She will to arrive at six.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Will is followed by the infinitive without to.

errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I don't think it will rain.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: It is more natural to make think negative.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with will or won't and the verb.
ejercicios.frase: Take an umbrella or you ___ (get) wet.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the use of will for predictions from the card. The clue is the structure “Take an umbrella or…”: it announces what will happen if the advice is ignored, a prediction about the future. That is why you will get wet or, contracted, you'll get wet. After will comes the infinitive without to or -s.
ejercicios.traduccion: Llévate un paraguas o te mojarás.

errores_previstos.explicacion: With you the present does not take -s, and besides, here you need will for the prediction: will get.
Will is followed by the infinitive without to.
After will the verb does not take -s.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the negative form of will.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the negative from the table in the card: won't (will not) + infinitive. The clue is “Don't worry”: someone is being reassured with a negative prediction. The verb hurt is in the infinitive without -s, even though the subject is the injection. Both the contracted and the full form are accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tranquilo, la inyección no te va a doler.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After won't the verb has no -s.
The present describes a general truth; to reassure someone about what is going to happen, use won't.
Will not is followed by the infinitive without to.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with will and the verb.
ejercicios.frase: A: I'm thirsty. B: Wait, I ___ (get) you some water.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the use of will for offers and spontaneous decisions. The clue is that B reacts to what they have just heard (“I'm thirsty”): they decide at that moment and make an offer. That is why I'll get you some water. In Spanish we use the present (“te traigo”), but in English the present sounds incomplete here.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Offer decided on the spot: will.
ejercicios.traduccion: A: Tengo sed. B: Espera, te traigo agua.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A literal translation of the Spanish present “te traigo”; in English an offer decided on the spot takes will.
Going to indicates a plan decided earlier; here the decision comes on hearing that the other person is thirsty.
Will is followed by the infinitive without to.

ejercicios.explicacion: The table in the card includes Shall I / Shall we + infinitive for offering or suggesting. The clue is the first person I in a question in which the speaker offers to do something. In that case, use shall, not will. “Will I turn on the heating?” would ask for a prediction, not make an offer.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To offer with I, use Shall I...?

errores_previstos.explicacion: Will I…? asks about what will happen; it does not offer help. To offer, use Shall I…?
A literal translation of the Spanish present “¿pongo?”; in English the offer is Shall I…?

ejercicios.frase: A: There's no milk. B: OK, I ___ some.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card contrasts will, for decisions made at the moment, with going to, for decisions made earlier. The clue is that B finds out now that there is no milk and reacts with “OK”: the decision is spontaneous. That is why I'll buy some.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Decision made on hearing the information: will.
ejercicios.traduccion: A: No hay leche. B: Vale, compro.

por_opcion.'ll buy: Correct: will for a decision made on hearing the information.
por_opcion.'m going to buy: Incorrect here: going to indicates that the decision had already been made, which does not fit finding out at that moment.
por_opcion.buy: Incorrect: the present simple does not express an immediate decision about the future (a literal translation of Spanish “compro”).

ejercicios.frase: I don't think they ___ the contract.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that with I think the negative usually goes on think: I don't think + will. The clue is that the sentence already begins with I don't think, so the negation is already expressed and the verb in the subordinate clause is affirmative: will sign. Repeating the negation would be a double negative.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With I don't think, the negation is already on think.
ejercicios.traduccion: No creo que firmen el contrato.

por_opcion.will sign: Correct: the negation goes on don't think and the prediction stays affirmative.
por_opcion.won't sign: Incorrect: with I don't think it would be a double negative and would change the meaning (“I don't think they won't sign”).
por_opcion.signing: Incorrect: the finite verb is missing; after I don't think comes a full clause.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the appropriate future form.
ejercicios.frase: I've already decided: I ___ (buy) a new laptop next week.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card points out that if the decision was already made before speaking, going to is used, not will. The clue is “I've already decided”: it is a previous plan. That is why I am going to buy, or contracted, I'm going to buy. Will would suggest that the decision is being made at that moment, which contradicts the first part of the sentence.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Plan decided in advance: going to, not will.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ya lo he decidido: la semana que viene me voy a comprar un portátil nuevo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Will expresses a decision made at the moment of speaking, and the sentence says it had already been decided: am going to buy.
The present simple is not used for personal future plans (except for fixed timetables).
The verb be is missing: I am going to buy (or I'm going to buy).

ejercicios.explicacion: The card stresses that after will comes the infinitive without to and without -s, for all persons. The clue is the third person she, which would take -s in the present, but not with will. Maybe introduces an uncertain prediction. That is why will call.

por_opcion.will call: Correct: will + infinitive without to or -s.
por_opcion.will calls: Incorrect: after will the verb does not take -s, even though the subject is she.
por_opcion.will to call: Incorrect: will is not followed by to.

ejercicios.enunciado: Turn the sentence into a question.
ejercicios.frase: The train will be on time.
respuestas: Will the train be on time?
ejercicios.explicacion: The table in the card gives the question: Will + subject + infinitive. To transform the affirmative sentence, just put will before the subject the train; the rest of the sentence does not change. Do or does is not used, because will is already an auxiliary.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Does the train will be on time?
errores_previstos.explicacion: Will is already an auxiliary; it is not combined with does.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Will the train is on time?
errores_previstos.explicacion: After will comes the infinitive be, not the finite form is.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Will be the train on time?
errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject goes immediately after will, before the verb be.

ejercicios.enunciado: Make the sentence negative with won't.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the negative from the card: won't + infinitive. The instruction asks you to use won't, the contraction of will not. Replace will with won't and the infinitive finish stays the same. Don't is not used, because will is an auxiliary.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We don't will finish before Friday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Will is an auxiliary and is made negative itself; it does not take don't.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We won't to finish before Friday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Won't is followed by the infinitive without to.
After won't comes the infinitive, finish, not the past.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card indicates that after will the infinitive does not take -s. The clue is the third person he, which tempts you to add -s as in the present. But the verb that goes with will does not change: He will come back, or contracted, He'll come back.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: after will, do not add -s.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He will to come back soon.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Will no va seguido de to.
The contraction does not change the rule: after 'll the verb has no -s.

ejercicios.frase: I promise I don't forget your birthday.
respuestas: I promise I won't forget your birthday.
I promise I will not forget your birthday.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card includes promises among the uses of will: I won't tell anyone. The clue is I promise: what is promised is in the future and in English it is expressed with will or won't. In Spanish we can say “te prometo que no me olvido”, in the present, but in English don't forget sounds like a general truth. That is why won't forget.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Promises about the future are expressed with will / won't.
ejercicios.traduccion: Te prometo que no me olvidaré de tu cumpleaños.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I promise I don't forget your birthday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: a promise about the future takes won't.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I promise I won't to forget your birthday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Won't is followed by the infinitive without to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I promise I won't forgot your birthday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After won't comes the infinitive, forget, not the past.

respuestas: I think it will be sunny
ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives I think + will as the typical form of a prediction based on opinion. The order is I think, and then the predicted clause with its own subject it, will and the infinitive be with the adjective sunny. In English the subject it is compulsory, even though Spanish “hará sol” has none.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I think will be it sunny
errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject it goes before will, not after it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I will think it be sunny
errores_previstos.explicacion: Will goes with the prediction (it will be), not with think.

ejercicios.enunciado: Put the words in order to make a question.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card includes will for requests: Will you…, please? The question is formed with will before the subject you, followed by the infinitive help and the object me. It is a direct request; with would or could it would sound more polite.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject you goes right after will and before the verb help.
The roles are reversed: the person who helps (you) is the subject and me is the object.

descripcion_larga_es: Will + infinitive is the so-called future simple, but in English it is not the “default” future: it is used for predictions based on opinion, decisions made on the spot, offers, promises and requests. Its form is the same for all persons. It is difficult for Spanish speakers because Spanish makes offers and promises in the present (“te ayudo”, “no se lo digo a nadie”) and because plans already decided take going to.

contexto.que_es: Will is a modal verb which, followed by the infinitive without to, expresses the future with specific nuances: prediction or opinion, spontaneous decision, offer, promise and request. Its negative is won't (will not) and in questions it is inverted with the subject. To offer or suggest with I or we, use shall.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is essential for offering help, promising, asking for something or giving an opinion about the future, situations that come up constantly in conversation. Using the present where English requires will (“I help you”) sounds odd or even impolite, and using will for a plan already decided suggests that the decision is improvised. The contrast between will and going to is tested a lot in exams.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When you decide something on the spot (The phone's ringing. I'll get it), offer (I'll carry that), promise (I won't be late) or predict with I think, probably or I'm sure. Signals: a reaction to something just heard, verbs of opinion, promise formulas. Spanish speakers tend to use the present in offers and promises, and to add to or -s after will.
